title: Nick Chubb Announces Retirement After Eight-Season Career
seoTitle: Nick Chubb retires after eight seasons
subtitle: Four-time Pro Bowler and four 1,000‑yard seasons bids farewell to the league.
excerpt: Running back Nick Chubb, one of the NFL's biggest names of the past decade, announced his retirement on Friday, ending an eight‑season career.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Running back Nick Chubb, one of the biggest names of the last decade in the NFL, announced his retirement this Friday after eight seasons in the league. The 30‑year‑old's decision, highlighted by being a four‑time Pro Bowler and posting four consecutive seasons with over 1,000 rushing yards, is among the most discussed topics, marking the end of a remarkable journey in American football.

A Career Marked by Excellence

Selected with the 35th overall pick by the Cleveland Browns in the 2018 NFL Draft, Nick Chubb quickly established himself as a game‑changer. In his rookie year he amassed 1,145 scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns. He then solidified his reputation with four straight seasons above the 1,000‑yard rushing mark, reaching 1,525 yards in 2022, his best performance ever.

Across 100 games, Chubb finishes his career with 7,349 rushing yards, 1,109 receiving yards and 59 touchdowns. His consistency and production power made him one of the most respected running backs of his generation.

The Impact of Injuries

Despite a stellar career, Chubb faced significant injury challenges. In 2015, while playing at Georgia, he suffered a severe knee injury. Years later, in 2023, now in the NFL, he endured another devastating knee injury in the first two games of the season, which required a second, arduous rehabilitation. He returned in 2024 after the 2023 injury.

Nick Chubb's Words

The retirement announcement came from Chubb on Instagram, in a message he described as “the day I have been avoiding for a while.” He reflected on his journey and the importance of health as he steps away from the sport.

  • “The twelve‑year‑old Nick Chubb could never have imagined this day, and the thirty‑year‑old is wondering where all the time went. I’ve known this for a while, but I’m finally ready to share that I’m done playing football.”
  • “Dealing with injuries was something that wasn’t part of the plan. The only thing I could control after hurting my knee twice was to get up, get back to work, and get back on the field. And I managed to do that both times.”
  • “There’s a life waiting for you after football too. And health is true wealth. I’m ending my career in a great place.”

The Athlete’s Legacy

Even though injuries deprived him of a few additional deep playoff runs later in his career, Nick Chubb delivered a stellar and standout tenure in the NFL. His resilience in overcoming serious injuries and his on‑field consistency secure his place as one of the most memorable running backs of the league over the past decade. He retires healthy and on his own terms at age 30.

With information from NFL.com, Fox News.
